info.name: ZoikoTax API (v1)
info.description:
**Generated from `contracts/openapi/ztax.v1.yaml` — do not edit.**

Run `npm run postman` in `contracts/` after changing the contract or the overlay. A hand edit fails CI (ADR-0010 §2.1): a hand-maintained collection is a second, kinder statement of what the API is.

Contract digest: `sha256:2815bbc9532f029090f92872491b136c7177550d6505cfd2c3468a598d05a93b`

Import and run; there is no environment to select. `baseUrl` defaults to the local cell and every other value rides along as a collection variable.

## Before you run it

Bring the stack up (`docker compose up --build`), which bootstraps the `acme` tenant and its administrator. Then run the whole collection: `02 · Sign in` opens the session everything below depends on.

Folder `90` is the one worth reading. Each request there sends something a well-behaved client would never send, and each asserts a control from the ADRs against an endpoint that exists today.

Folder `99` records the determination surface, which is specified and not built. Its paths are listed in `pendingPaths`, so a 404 there reports as *not implemented yet* rather than as a wall of red.

item.name: 00 · Health — served, and deliberately not in the contract
item.description:
An orchestrator calls these; no SDK does. They carry no session, their bodies are plain text, and declaring them in the contract would generate client methods nobody should call and make a liveness probe a compatibility commitment (ADR-0010 §2.6).

They are added by the generator rather than derived from the contract, and `contract_test.go` keeps the same exception register on the server side.

request.description: Liveness: the process is running and can serve. It touches no dependency on purpose — a liveness probe that failed when the database was down would get the process killed, which does not fix a database and does lose the in-memory content bundle.

Readiness: this replica can take traffic right now. Unlike liveness it does check the cell store, because a replica that cannot reach it should leave the rotation rather than serve one 503 per caller.

item.description: What this deployment can actually do, before you have a session.

item.name: GET /v1/capabilities — Report this deployment's effective capability

request.description:
Report this deployment's effective capability

Effective capability, not entitlement: the intersection of content
state, security, QA and commercial entitlement (ADR-0010 §2.6).

Unauthenticated, because a client needs to know whether a cell can serve
it before it has a session, and because an integration diagnosing a
problem should not need a credential to report which cell and which
content bundle it reached.

`content` is absent in a cell with no bundle loaded, which is a
legitimate deployment before A4. Absent rather than null: "no content"
and "content with no identity" are different facts (ADR-0011 P3).

response.name: 200 · A cell before A4, with a worked pack loaded
200 · A cell deployed with no content bundle

item.name: 02 · Sign in
item.description: Opens the session every folder below depends on. The response carries no token — the session is an `HttpOnly` cookie Postman's cookie jar keeps for you.

request.description:
Open a session

Exchanges a tenant slug, an email address and a password for an opaque
session cookie.

The response carries **no token**. The session identifier is in a
`__Host-`-prefixed, `HttpOnly`, `SameSite=Strict` cookie that JavaScript
cannot read, which is why the browser client has nothing to store and
nothing to leak (ADR-0019 C8, ADR-0020).

A failure does not distinguish an unknown subject from a wrong password.
The difference is an account-enumeration oracle and a caller can do
nothing with it, so both are `INVALID_CREDENTIALS`.

// one cannot be revoked. The absence of it here is the design.

request.description:

item.name: 90 · Contract conformance — what arrives that should not
item.description:
Requests a well-behaved client would never send. Each asserts a control, and each runs against an endpoint that exists today — so a green row here is evidence rather than an aspiration.

These need a session: run `01 · Sign in` first, or run the whole collection.

item.name: Unknown field is rejected, not ignored

request.description:
ADR-0011 §2.1 P5 at the transport boundary.

Silently dropping an undeclared field would let two different requests digest identically, which is exactly the property an idempotency record depends on (ADR-0013 §2.4). It is also the common shape of a real integration bug: a client sends `displayname` where the contract says `displayName`, and a server that ignores it creates a user with no display name and reports success.

request.description:
ADR-0011 §2.1 P3.

"Explicitly cleared" and "not supplied" are different facts with different consequences, and a canonical form that collapses them erases the difference from the evidence too. So `null` is an error rather than something to normalise.

item.name: 98 · Destructive — run deliberately, not as part of a pass
item.description:
`changePassword` revokes every session for the subject, including the calling one — a password change is what you do when a credential is believed compromised, and leaving other sessions alive would defeat it.

It also leaves the bootstrap administrator on `{{newPassword}}`, which the collection's `adminPassword` no longer names. Run it when you mean to, then update `adminPassword` or re-bootstrap the tenant.

item.name: POST /v1/auth/password — Change the current subject's password

request.description:
Change the current subject's password

Verifies the current password and replaces it.

**Every session for this subject is revoked, including this one.** A
password change is the action taken when a credential is believed
compromised, and leaving other sessions alive would defeat it. The
client is signed out and must sign in again.

item.name: 99 · Awaiting the determination surface
item.description:
The surface `ZTAX-INT-001` specifies and ADR-0010 §2.5 names: quotes, commit, adjust, refund, decisions, replay, classifications, obligations, batches and jobs.

None of it exists, none of it is in the contract, and the payloads below are derived from the domain model in the ADRs rather than from a published contract — so field names will change. They are here because the *controls* they assert are decided even though the endpoints are not, and because W2 lane K should have something to run on the day it builds them.

These paths are in `pendingPaths`, so a 404 is reported as "not implemented yet" rather than as a failure.

item.name: Idempotency · 1 · first commit with a fixed key

request.description: ADR-0013 §2.4. The first of four: this one establishes the record, and requests 2 to 4 are the interesting ones.
Must return the *original* response, not a new one. A retry that produced a second decision would be a second fiscal record for one transaction, which is the Critical risk in Build Plan §8.

Must be a 409 `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSE` and must not execute (ADR-0013 §2.4).

Replaying the original response would be worse than either alternative: the caller would believe the amount it sent was the amount recorded.

`Idempotency-Key` is mandatory on `:commit`, `:adjust`, `:refund` and `POST /v1/batches` (ADR-0013 §2.1). Rejected before any work begins.

The contract lint already enforces the other half of this: when those paths are added, an operation that does not declare a required `Idempotency-Key` header fails `npm run lint`.

item.name: Canonical form · a fiscal amount sent as a JSON number

request.description:
**The request in this collection that matters most.**

`"netAmount": 45.0` must be rejected, never coerced. A 2xx here is a Critical finding rather than a test failure: RFC 8785 serializes JSON numbers through IEEE 754 doubles (ADR-0011 §1.1), so an amount that is ever a JSON number has lost precision before canonicalization sees it — and the loss is invisible, because 45.0 survives and 0.1 does not.

The body is raw text rather than a structured one, because the whole point is to send a token a correct client cannot produce.
